_readme: Scope boundary for agents. Work on one feature at a time. status: todo | in_progress | done | superseded. Lower priority number first; skip items whose depends_on are not done. Optional fields: epic (A prioritization/freshness, B dependency health, C reports and repo health, D tools that act, E foundations), size (S/M/L), depends_on, notes, labels (triage roles, docs/agents/triage-labels.md), parent and assignee (wayfinding, docs/agents/issue-tracker.md). Set done only after the Definition of Done in docs/WORKFLOW.md passes and put the commands/results in evidence.

features.title: Map: in-app auth for a public single-user deployment
acceptance: Frontier empty; E-002 re-scoped and ready to build
features.evidence: 2026-10-30: frontier empty; E-002 re-scoped, E-003 added.
features.notes:
DESTINATION: Auth approach for a public single-user deployment decided, and E-002 re-scoped to match so it is ready to build.
NOTES: Audience is the owner only. Auth must be in-app (a network gate such as Tailscale/Cloudflare Access was ruled out). Uploads keep their separate bearer-token surface. Consult ARCHITECTURE.md#security and E-002.
DECISIONS SO FAR:
- W-002 Research: Auth.js v5 fit for this stack, and minimal alternatives: Auth.js v5 (beta.32 exact pin) fits Next 16.4.1 technically, but it reads process.env.AUTH_* (clashes with env() rule), GitHub OAuth needs outbound HTTP from the web app (clashes with 'external HTTP only from src/worker/', needs ADR/exception), JWT sessions can't be revoked, and CVE-2026-73421 is fail-open (gate on auth?.user). A hand-rolled jose gate is Next's documented pattern (~150-300 lines est.). Proxy matcher must cover pages and GET /api/v1/*, not upload POSTs. Detail in W-002 notes.
- W-003 Auth mechanism for a single owner: GitHub OAuth via next-auth v4, one owner id, others see nothing, 7-day cookie; see ADR 0001.
- W-004 Enforcement boundary: gate all pages + GET /api/v1/*, proxy plus requireOwner() with a coverage test, 503 fail-closed in production (ALLOW_OPEN_READS opt-out).
- W-005 Roles: none; single owner, others denied; E-002 re-scoped and split, ops moved to E-003.
NOT YET SPECIFIED (cleared; now steps in E-003): live GitHub OAuth round trip and behaviour under compose read_only; how long next-auth v4 gets security patches; NEXTAUTH_URL/cookie-name handling behind TRUST_PROXY; test strategy (unit + e2e) for authed pages; public-deploy hardening checklist (TLS, worker SSRF audit, rate limit across replicas); how E-002 splits into build vs ops.
OUT OF SCOPE: multi-user/team visibility and roles; DORA metrics (C-006).

features.title: Research: Auth.js v5 fit for this stack, and minimal alternatives
acceptance: Answer recorded in notes and gist appended to W-001 Decisions so far

features.notes: QUESTION: Does Auth.js v5 fit this repo's Next.js version (middleware/proxy, JWT sessions with no DB adapter, standalone Docker build, known CVEs)? What would a minimal signed-cookie single-user gate cost by comparison? Findings go in the research/auth-fit branch. ANSWER (2026-10-30): Auth.js v5 (beta.32 exact pin) fits Next 16.4.1 technically, but it reads process.env.AUTH_* (clashes with env() rule), GitHub OAuth needs outbound HTTP from the web app (clashes with 'external HTTP only from src/worker/', needs ADR/exception), JWT sessions can't be revoked, and CVE-2026-73421 is fail-open (gate on auth?.user). A hand-rolled jose gate is Next's documented pattern (~150-300 lines est.). Proxy matcher must cover pages and GET /api/v1/*, not upload POSTs. Full findings: docs/research/auth-fit.md on branch research/auth-fit.

features.title: Auth mechanism for a single owner
acceptance: Answer recorded in notes and gist appended to W-001 Decisions so far
features.evidence: 2026-10-30: decided with the user in session; research on branch research/next-auth-v4 (smoke app, no live GitHub round trip).
features.notes: QUESTION: GitHub OAuth with a one-login allow-list, password/passkey, or generic OIDC? How is the owner identity configured via env()? ANSWER (2026-10-30): GitHub OAuth via next-auth v4 (stable latest), pinned exactly; config from env() (public URL assigned to NEXTAUTH_URL from env(); never set AUTH_TRUST_HOST). Owner = one numeric GitHub id in env, compared as a string, re-checked on every request in proxy and requireOwner(); empty = nobody. Others can sign in but get a plain 'Access denied' page (their login + sign-out link), nothing stored. isAllowed() is the seam for future grants. Session: 7-day cookie, set BOTH session.maxAge and jwt.maxAge to 604800 (jwt default is 30d); revoke by changing the owner id or rotating NEXTAUTH_SECRET. Reuse the existing in-memory rate limiter on auth routes. Proxy: custom proxy() with getToken, JSON 401 for /api/*, gate everything except upload POSTs (branch on method inside the proxy). GitHub egress exception recorded in docs/adr/0001-github-oauth-egress-from-web-app.md. Detail: docs/research/next-auth-v4.md on branch research/next-auth-v4.

features.title: Enforcement boundary: which surfaces are gated and where
acceptance: Answer recorded in notes and gist appended to W-001 Decisions so far
features.evidence: 2026-10-30: decided with the user in session after listing routes in src/app.
features.notes: QUESTION: Which of pages, GET /api/v1/*, health and static assets require a session? Enforced in middleware or in src/server/? Fail-closed in production like UPLOAD_TOKENS, or off by default as E-002 states? Upload POST stays bearer-token. ANSWER (2026-10-30): Gated: every page and every GET /api/v1/*. Open: /api/auth/*, /api/healthz, static assets (/_next/*, icon), and the two bearer-token routes (POST /api/v1/sboms, DELETE /api/v1/projects/[id]) which the proxy passes through by method+path to their existing UPLOAD_TOKENS check. Two layers: proxy (cheap token check; pages redirect to sign-in, /api/* JSON 401; unknown paths gated too) plus requireOwner() in src/server/auth.ts called at the top of every GET handler and page; a test enumerates all route.ts/page.tsx and fails if one lacks the guard or an allow-list entry. Not put in inventory.ts read functions (signature churn). Fail-closed: in production with auth not fully configured (owner id, secret, GitHub client id/secret, NEXTAUTH_URL) reads return 503; ALLOW_OPEN_READS=true opts out (mirrors ALLOW_OPEN_UPLOADS); dev/test off by default. Signed-out: minimal sign-in page with one GitHub button, no auto-redirect; non-owner sees Access denied page; API 401 without session, 403 for non-owner.

features.title: Map: monitor the underlying k3s/Ubuntu host from the dashboard
acceptance: Frontier empty; host-monitoring work broken into buildable features in features.json
features.notes:
DESTINATION: A decided design for showing the freshness and vulnerability posture of the Ubuntu droplet running k3s in this dashboard, broken into buildable features in features.json.
NOTES: Read-only reporting; no metrics, uptime or remediation. The droplet pushes data in (systemd timer and/or k3s CronJob with an upload token); the dashboard holds no credentials into the server and the app never reaches out (only src/worker does external HTTP via FetchFn). One droplet today, but each host is named in the data (project of kind host, e.g. host:<name>). Reuse and depend on B-004 (image scans), C-001 (generic report upload) and B-001 (EOL) instead of building a parallel pipeline; map only host-specific deltas. Consult ARCHITECTURE.md and CONTEXT.md.
DECISIONS SO FAR:
- W-007 Research: OSV and Ubuntu package data for host CVEs: feasible via OSV, but the worker must query by source package + release ecosystem and needs a dpkg version comparator; deps.dev is useless for deb, so 'latest' comes from apt. Three items unverified (see W-007).
- W-008 Research: signals for host and k3s freshness: collector reads apt-get -s upgrade (security by origin suite), reboot-required with mtime, Pro/ESM status, os-release; worker fetches Ubuntu EOL from endoflife.date and k3s latest patch per minor from update.k3s.io channels; k3s minor EOL has no source (upstream kubernetes as proxy); Pro-less LTS past support is a false all-clear risk.
NOT YET SPECIFIED:
- Silence detection: how a stopped collector shows as stale (heartbeat / last-reported age and thresholds) and whether it needs D-002 notifications.
- Cluster workload inventory: which images are actually running in k3s (vs. images declared in repos) and how they link to B-004/B-005.
- Stale/red thresholds for pending security updates, kernel age, reboot-required, k3s patch lag.
- Per-host upload tokens vs. the single shared token.
- UI surface: host in the projects list vs. a dedicated Hosts view and overview tiles.
- Build order against B-001/B-004/C-001 once the data shape is known.
OUT OF SCOPE: metrics/uptime/alerting on resource use (Prometheus territory); automated patching or any remediation; the dashboard having SSH/kubeconfig access; fleet management beyond naming hosts.

features.title: Research: OSV and Ubuntu package data for host CVEs
acceptance: Answer recorded in notes and gist appended to W-006 Decisions so far
features.evidence: 2026-10-31: findings on branch research/host-osv-ubuntu (docs/research/host-osv-ubuntu.md), no PR.
features.notes:
QUESTION: What does OSV.dev expose for Ubuntu/Debian packages (ecosystem names per release, e.g. Ubuntu:22.04:LTS; USN/UBUNTU-CVE ids), how does Syft emit dpkg purls (pkg:deb/ubuntu/...?distro=), what version-comparison does dpkg need versus src/lib/version.ts, and is deps.dev useless for deb (so 'latest version' must come from apt's pending upgrades instead)? Findings only; cite primary sources.
ANSWER (2026-10-31): Feasible via OSV, but the worker must change. Ecosystems are per release (Ubuntu:22.04:LTS, Ubuntu:Pro:18.04:LTS); ids UBUNTU-CVE-*, USN-*, LSN-*. affected[].package.name is the SOURCE package (binaries in ecosystem_specific.binaries); USNs carry no severity (take it from the linked UBUNTU-CVE). Syft purl: pkg:deb/ubuntu/<bin>@<ver>?arch&upstream=<src>@<srcver>&distro=; only emitted when the distro is detected. Current toQuery in src/worker/osv.ts sends the binary name with no release, so libssl3 vs openssl would silently return nothing (looks clean when not). src/lib/version.ts is wrong for dpkg (strips +, no epoch, no ~); needs a Debian-policy comparator chosen by purl type. deps.dev has no deb support, so 'latest version' must come from apt --upgradable (agent's suggestion, not researched; W-008 covers it). Needed changes: store the host's Ubuntu release; query by source name/version + release ecosystem; dpkg comparator for fixedVersions and sorting; filter affected by release; group UBUNTU-CVE/USN/CVE ids. UNVERIFIED: whether OSV matches a bare Ubuntu ecosystem against suffixed ones; exact distro= value Syft emits on Ubuntu; purl spec deb section (URLs 404'd). Detail on branch research/host-osv-ubuntu.

features.title: Research: signals for host and k3s freshness
acceptance: Answer recorded in notes and gist appended to W-006 Decisions so far
features.evidence: 2026-10-31: findings on branch research/host-freshness-signals (docs/research/host-freshness-signals.md), no PR.
features.notes:
QUESTION: Which facts can a collector read to answer 'is this server up to date', and where does the 'latest' reference come from? Cover: apt pending upgrades split security/other (apt-get -s upgrade, apt list --upgradable, esm), /var/run/reboot-required and running vs installed kernel, unattended-upgrades state, Ubuntu release EOL (endoflife.date and its API), and k3s latest patch in the node's minor line (update.k3s.io release channels / GitHub releases) plus k3s minor EOL. Findings only; cite primary sources.
ANSWER (2026-10-31): HOST (collector) reads: pending upgrades via apt-get -s upgrade (read-only, no root; prefer apt-get over apt in scripts), classify each Inst line by origin suite (-security or esm = security); held-back and phased packages are not necessarily stale (security updates are never phased). Ubuntu Pro: pro security-status/status --format json; without Pro attached, '0 pending security' on an LTS past standard support is a false all-clear. Reboot: /var/run/reboot-required plus reboot-required.pkgs, push the flag's mtime too (auto-reboot defaults off). unattended-upgrades: 20auto-upgrades, 50unattended-upgrades, logs in /var/log/unattended-upgrades/; default origins security only. Also apt package-list age, /etc/os-release, k3s version string. WORKER (public reference) fetches: Ubuntu EOL from endoflife.date GET /api/v1/products/ubuntu/releases/<ver> (eolFrom, eoesFrom, isEol; sends etag, max-age=0, use conditional requests; no documented rate limit). k3s latest patch per minor from GET https://update.k3s.io/v1-release/channels (JSON shape observed live, not documented; GitHub releases API fallback, 60/h unauthenticated). endoflife.date has no k3s product; upstream kubernetes product is the practical EOL proxy (agent inference, k3s publishes no EOL policy). UNVERIFIED: Inst origin format, running-vs-installed kernel comparison, apt stamp file paths, exact unattended-upgrades log names, k3s version command, Livepatch; several Ubuntu Pro doc links 404. Open: verify on real 22.04/24.04 droplet; choose k3s EOL source (upstream vs SUSE support matrix, not fetched). Detail on branch research/host-freshness-signals.
